edges.description: The intermediate steps between the 7p14 allele and the vascular phenotype are entirely unknown; the edge records co-segregation of the haplotype with an HHT phenotype, not a characterized mechanism.
The mucocutaneous component of the dysplasia in this family produced nosebleeds and visible telangiectases that were milder and less frequent than in typical HHT.

The large-vessel component of the same dysplasia presents as arteriovenous malformation - the lesion that brought this family to clinical attention. Routed from the dysplasia node rather than from the mucocutaneous node because an AVM is not a mucocutaneous bleeding manifestation.
Bleeding from mucosal telangiectases of the nasal cavity presents as recurrent nosebleeds, mild and infrequent in this family.
The same mucocutaneous lesions are visible on examination as telangiectases, described here as subtle.

nodes.description: Arteriovenous malformation is the manifestation that brought the family to attention; the authors note that the underlying hereditary vascular dysplasia is easily missed when such a patient is evaluated for the AVM alone. The abstract does not specify the organ or organs involved, so the generic AVM term is used rather than the pulmonary or cerebral AVM terms carried in the OMIM clinical synopsis.

evidence.reference_title: A fourth locus for hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia maps to chromosome 7.
evidence.snippet: The features in this family that strongly suggest the presence of a hereditary, multisystem vascular dysplasia would be easily missed during the typical evaluation and management of a patient with an AVM.

nodes.description: The clinically distinguishing feature of the 7p14 family is not a different lesion type but a lower lesion burden: epistaxis and telangiectases were less severe than in typical HHT, to the point that the authors warn the diagnosis is easily missed and argue for a targeted family history in patients presenting with an AVM and only mild, infrequent nosebleeds and subtle telangiectases. Whether this attenuation is a property of the 7p14 allele or ordinary intrafamilial variability of HHT cannot be decided from a single family, and no severity comparison against genotyped HHT1/HHT2 cohorts has been published.

evidence.reference_title: A fourth locus for hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia maps to chromosome 7.
evidence.snippet: This family helps emphasize the need to obtain a very detailed, targeted medical and family history for even mild, infrequent but recurring nosebleed, subtle telangiectases.

nodes.description: The family mapping to 7p14 expresses the classic HHT lesion set - a hereditary, multisystem vascular dysplasia comprising mucocutaneous telangiectases and larger arteriovenous malformations. This node is curated at the level of the observed lesion class. Whether the abnormal vessels arise through the endothelial BMP/TGF-beta route established for ENG- and ACVRL1-related HHT is unknown and is deliberately not asserted here: no molecular study of this family or of the 7p14 interval exists, and the linkage data exclude the two genes for which that mechanism was worked out.

nodes.description: The proximal lesion is a germline variant segregating with disease within a 7 Mb interval on the short arm of chromosome 7 (7p14), between D7S2252 and D7S510. Neither the gene nor the variant class (coding, regulatory, structural) has been identified, so no molecular function, protein complex, or biological process can be assigned to this node. It is modelled explicitly as an unresolved trigger so that the downstream vascular phenotype is not attributed to a fabricated molecular cause - in particular, not to the BMP/TGF-beta co-receptor biology established for ENG and ACVRL1, which was excluded by linkage in this family.
